name: QuickPay.ge – Georgian Payments for WooCommerce
author: QuickPay Georgia

sections.description:
Scroll down for English

QuickPay.ge – Georgian Payments for WooCommerce თქვენს მაღაზიას აკავშირებს საქართველოში მოქმედ ყველა საგადახდო სისტემასთან ერთი ინტეგრაციით. თითოეული ბანკისთვის ცალკე კოდის დაწერის ან პლაგინის შეძენის ნაცვლად ერთხელ ინტეგრირდებით Quickpay.ge-სთან და იღებთ წვდომას ყველა საგადახდო სისტემაზე, რომლისთვისაც თქვენს ბიზნესს მერჩანტ ანგარიში აქვს.

მხარდაჭერილი საგადახდო მეთოდები:

  • საქართველოს ბანკი – ბარათით გადახდა
  • საქართველოს ბანკი – ონლაინ განვადება
  • საქართველოს ბანკი – ნაწილ-ნაწილ (Buy Now Pay Later)
  • თიბისი ბანკი – ბარათით გადახდა
  • თიბისი ბანკი – ონლაინ განვადება
  • კრედო ბანკი – ონლაინ განვადება
  • ლიბერთი ბანკი – ბარათით გადახდა
  • Keepz – ბარათით და მობაილ ბანკით გადახდა
  • Flitt – ბარათით და მობაილ ბანკით გადახდა
  • UniPay – ბარათით გადახდა
  • Fastoo – ბარათით გადახდა
  • CityPay – კრიპტოთი გადახდა
  • ElectraPay – კრიპტო გადახდები
  • Moka (United Payment) – ბარათით გადახდა
  • PayPal – ფეიფალით გადახდა (მხოლოდ დოლარი, ევრო)
  • Paysera – ბარათით გადახდა
  • საბანკო გადარიცხვა ავტომატური დადასტურებით
  • გადახდა კურიერთან (Cash on Delivery)

ძირითადი ფუნქციები:

  • ერთიანი გადახდის ღილაკი — ან
  • ცალკეული გადახდის ღილაკების რეჟიმი — თითოეული საგადახდო მეთოდი ცალკე ღილაკებით (ლოგოებით)
  • პროდუქტის გვერდზე სწრაფი ყიდვის ღილაკები
  • ყველა გადახდის სრული ანალიტიკა და კონტროლი QuickPay-ის ანგარიშში
  • WC Blocks-თან სრული თავსებადობა
  • WooCommerce HPOS თავსებადობა
  • ავტომატური თანხის დაბრუნება პირდაპირ შეკვეთის გვერდიდან
  • ვებჰუკების HMAC-SHA256 ხელმოწერით გადამოწმება
  • დეტალური Debug ლოგირება — WooCommerce → Status → Logs-ში
  • თავსებადია WPML / Polylang-თან — ყველა სტრიქონი მთარგმნელობადია მრავალენოვანი საიტებისთვის
  • ლაივ და სატესტო რეჟიმი
  • სრულად ქართული და ინგლისური ინტერფეისი

დამატებითი ინფორმაცია და დაყენების ინსტრუქცია: quickpay.ge/wordpress-plugin · quickpay.ge

English

QuickPay.ge – Georgian Payments for WooCommerce connects your store to every payment system operating in Georgia through a single integration. Instead of writing separate code for each bank — or buying a separate plugin — you integrate once with Quickpay.ge and get access to every gateway your business has a merchant account with.

Supported payment methods:

  • Bank of Georgia (BOG) — Card Payment
  • Bank of Georgia (BOG) — Online Installment
  • Bank of Georgia (BOG) — Part by Part (Buy Now Pay Later)
  • TBC Bank — Card Payment
  • TBC Bank — Online Installment
  • Credo Bank — Online Installment
  • Liberty Bank — Card Payment
  • Keepz — Card & Mobile Banking Payment
  • Flitt — Card & Mobile Banking Payment
  • UniPay — Card Payment
  • Fastoo — Card Payment
  • CityPay — Crypto Payment
  • ElectraPay — Crypto Payments
  • Moka (United Payment) — Card Payment
  • PayPal — PayPal Payment (USD, EUR only)
  • Paysera — Card Payment
  • Bank Transfer with Automatic Confirmation
  • Cash on Delivery

Key features:

  • Unified checkout button — single button that opens a branded Quickpay hosted payment page, or
  • Per-method buttons mode — each payment method as its own button (with logos)
  • Express “Buy Now” buttons on product pages
  • Full payment analytics and control from your QuickPay dashboard
  • WC Blocks compatible — works with the modern Cart and Checkout blocks
  • HPOS compatible — fully supports WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage
  • Automatic refunds — trigger partial or full refunds directly from the WC order screen
  • Webhook verification — all incoming webhooks are HMAC-SHA256 signed and verified
  • Debug logging — detailed logs written to WooCommerce → Status → Logs
  • WPML / Polylang ready — all translatable strings registered for multilingual sites
  • Live and Test mode
  • Georgian + English — full UI translation in both languages

How it works:

  1. Merchant signs up at quickpay.ge and connects their bank merchant accounts
  2. Install this plugin and enter your API key — see the WooCommerce integration guide for step-by-step setup
  3. Customers pay on the Quickpay hosted payment page (qpy.ge) — no card data touches your server
  4. A signed webhook confirms payment and WooCommerce order is updated automatically

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.3+
  • WooCommerce 8.0+
  • PHP 7.4+
  • A Quickpay.ge merchant account with at least one active gateway subscription

Privacy Policy

This plugin communicates with the Quickpay.ge API (api.quickpay.ge) to:

  • Verify API key credentials and fetch available payment gateways
  • Create payment requests and retrieve payment status
  • Process refunds

Payment data (customer name, email, order amount) is transmitted to Quickpay.ge as part of the payment creation request. Please refer to the Quickpay.ge Privacy Policy for details on how payment data is handled.

Separately, this plugin sends three tiers of non-payment data to Quickpay.ge:

Always sent (no setting to disable): this site’s domain and its plugin/WordPress/WooCommerce/PHP versions, on activation, deactivation, and a weekly heartbeat. This is how Quickpay knows the plugin is installed — including before it’s connected to an account — and is used to prioritize security and compatibility fixes. It never includes your API key or any customer/order data.

Extended data (opt-in, off by default): enable “Extended Usage Data” in Quickpay → Settings → Advanced to also share your installed plugins, active theme, and site environment (HPOS/multisite status, locale) on the weekly heartbeat. Not required for the plugin to function.

Diagnostic reports (on-demand only, never automatic): from Quickpay → Logs & System Status, you can generate a snapshot of your Quickpay configuration and environment (connectivity check, order/display mode, enabled gateways, currency settings, cron health) to send to support when troubleshooting an issue. You review it on screen before anything is sent.

No data is sent to any third-party service other than Quickpay.ge.
sections.installation:
Automatic installation

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New in your WordPress admin
  2. Search for “QuickPay.ge – Georgian Payments for WooCommerce”
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate

Manual installation

  1. Download the plugin zip from quickpay.ge
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin
  3. Upload the zip, then activate

Configuration

  1. Go to Quickpay → Settings in the WordPress admin sidebar
  2. Enter your API key from your Quickpay.ge dashboard
  3. Click Test Connection — the plugin will fetch your available gateways
  4. Copy the Webhook URL shown and paste it into your Quickpay.ge dashboard → Webhooks
  5. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Payments and enable Quickpay
sections.faq:
Do I need a Quickpay.ge account?

Yes. The plugin is a client for the Quickpay.ge payment gateway API. You need a merchant account at quickpay.ge to use it.

Does card data pass through my server?

No. Customers complete payment on the Quickpay hosted payment page (qpy.ge), which is hosted entirely by Quickpay. No card numbers, CVVs, or sensitive payment data ever touch your WordPress server.

Which Georgian banks are supported?

Bank of Georgia (BOG), TBC Bank, Credo Bank, and others — see the full list in the plugin description. Available gateways depend on which subscriptions are active on your Quickpay.ge account.

Does it work with WooCommerce Blocks?

Yes. The plugin registers a native WooCommerce Blocks payment integration and declares full cart/checkout blocks compatibility.

Does it support HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage)?

Yes. The plugin declares custom_order_tables compatibility and uses WC_Order objects throughout.

Can I test payments without real money?

Yes. Use a test API key (starts with qpk_test_) — test keys route through sandbox environments and never hit real gateway APIs.

How are refunds handled?

You can issue full or partial refunds directly from the WooCommerce order screen. The plugin calls the Quickpay API which forwards the refund request to the original gateway. Refund confirmation arrives via webhook and is recorded in WooCommerce automatically.

What is “Mode B” / express checkout?

Mode B (Express) lets you add “Buy Now” buttons directly on product pages. When a customer clicks, a Quickpay payment is created immediately and the customer is redirected to pay — no cart step required. The WooCommerce order is created automatically when payment is confirmed.

Where do I find the webhook URL?

Go to Quickpay → Settings in your WP admin. The webhook URL is shown in the Connection section. Copy it and add it in your Quickpay.ge dashboard under Settings → Webhooks.

Does it support installment payment display?

Yes. In Mode B (product page express buttons), you can display static installment labels (e.g. “from 50 GEL/month”) configured in the plugin settings.
sections.changelog:
2.9.25

  • Fixed: The WordPress.org listing screenshots and icon were being bundled into the plugin’s downloadable files; they’re now excluded as intended

2.9.24

  • Changed: Plugin renamed to “QuickPay.ge – Georgian Payments for WooCommerce” for clarity in the WordPress plugin directory

2.9.23

  • Changed: Updated bank names and formatting in the Georgian plugin description

2.9.22

  • Changed: Rewrote the plugin description with a full bilingual (Georgian + English) overview and the complete list of supported gateways, including Liberty Card and ElectraPay which were previously missing from the listing

2.9.21

  • Fixed: An in-place update (as opposed to a fresh install) doesn’t trigger WordPress’s plugin activation hook, so sites that updated straight from an older version without ever toggling “Share anonymous usage data” would never pick up the base telemetry heartbeat added in 2.9.18. The plugin now detects a version change on its next admin page load and schedules the heartbeat then, regardless of how the update happened

2.9.20

  • Changed: Payment method eligibility, webhook authentication, and telemetry handling have been reviewed and hardened. For full release notes on earlier versions, contact Quickpay.ge support.

2.9.19

  • Added: WordPress.org directory listing base banner (banner-772x250.png) — the @2x-only banner previously shipped wasn’t showing up on the plugin’s public page/search cards without it
  • Added: Screenshot #6 (express button dark/outline style variants) caption in the directory listing
